title: How to Turn Google Slides into a Narrated Video (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: Turn Google Slides into a Narrated Video
slides.notes: Your lectures already live in Google Slides. The slides carry the visuals, and the speaker notes carry your words. Here's how to turn them into a narrated video.

slides.title: Narrate slides instead of recording lectures
bullets: No studio, microphone or clean run needed
Fix a mistake by editing a line
Students pause and replay at their pace
slides.notes: Recording live needs a quiet room and a clean run. With narrated slides, fixing a mistake means editing one line of text, then making the video again.

slides.title: Write speaker notes for the ear
bullets: Before: Sampling bias - convenience samples - eg uni students
After: Here's the problem with convenience samples.
Short sentences, one idea at a time
slides.notes: Reminder notes won't work as a script. Write full sentences, the way you'd explain the slide to a student sitting right next to you.

slides.title: Download as .pptx, then choose a voice
bullets: Swap embedded videos for a still image
Choose a voice and speaking speed
slides.notes: In Google Slides, download your deck as a PowerPoint file. Upload it, choose a voice and speed that sounds natural, and keep captions on for every student.

slides.title: Watch the whole video before sharing
bullets: Notes that read awkwardly out loud
slides.notes: Listen for mispronounced names and awkward lines, then fix them in your speaker notes. A twenty-slide segment becomes a focused video of roughly seven to ten minutes.

slides.title: Ordinary slides in, extraordinary video out
bullets: Basic: try it, with a watermark
slides.notes: Ordinary slides in, extraordinary video out. On Pro, a.i. directs your lecture video, timing each scene to your narration. Try Basic first at powerpoint2vid.com.
